# Value Pyramid

`sales.mm.core.value_pyramid` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core** · kind **mental_model**

> Sorts every claim a seller can make into the tier of buyer outcome it serves, so that the claim is aimed at a person who is actually measured on it. Value is not a property of the product; it is a relation between what the product does and what a specific person is accountable for. The same feature is a differentiator to one seat on the committee and noise to the next.


## Dimensions

| Dimension | Asks | Weak signal | Strong signal | Objects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Conformance (table stakes) | Does the offer clear the bar required to be considered at all — security, data residency, insurance, accessibility, payment terms? | "We can probably be flexible on that." Nobody has read the questionnaire, and the answer will arrive in legal review three weeks after the forecast was committed.  | Security review completed, DPA countersigned, insurance certificate on file — all before the commercial conversation, because none of them are negotiable and all of them take longer than the seller expects.  | `sales.obj.core.risk`, `sales.obj.core.contract`, `sales.obj.core.account` |
| Functional value | What does the product do that the current way of working cannot, stated as a capability rather than a feature name? | A feature list with no comparison. Buyers cannot evaluate a capability in isolation; they evaluate it against what they do today, and if you do not supply the comparison they will invent an unflattering one.  | The buyer restates the capability unprompted in their own words, and names the manual step it removes.  | `sales.obj.core.business_need`, `sales.obj.core.pain_point`, `sales.obj.core.competitor` |
| Operational value | What changes in how the work actually runs on a Monday, for which team, and how many people feel it? | Time savings expressed per user per week with no headcount behind them. Two hours a week saved by four people is not a business case, it is a rounding error with a slide.  | A named process, its current cycle time, the number of people in it, and the owner of that team agreeing the number is right.  | `sales.obj.core.stakeholder`, `sales.obj.core.pain_point`, `sales.obj.core.persona` |
| Economic value | Which line, on whose P&L, moves — from what baseline, by how much, by when? | A multiple with no denominator — "10x ROI". Finance discounts unsourced multiples to zero, and the seller never learns because the deal dies as "no decision" months later.  | A one-page case the buyer's own finance function has already amended. Amendments are the proof of engagement; a case returned untouched was never read.  | `sales.obj.core.budget`, `sales.obj.core.decision_maker`, `sales.obj.core.proposal`, `sales.obj.core.pricing` |
| Strategic value | Which published company priority does this advance, and which executive is accountable for that priority this year? | A priority lifted from the annual report and repeated back verbatim. Every vendor in the evaluation read the same report; quoting it signals research, not insight.  | An executive sponsor connects the purchase to a target they are personally measured on, in a meeting the seller did not have to chase.  | `sales.obj.core.company`, `sales.obj.core.account`, `sales.obj.core.opportunity` |
| Personal value | What does each individual gain if this succeeds, and lose if it fails — career risk, credit, workload, standing? | No answer at all, because the seller has never considered it. This is the tier every vendor deck omits and a large share of enterprise deals turn on.  | The champion says some version of "I need this to work" — they have attached their own name to the outcome, which is the only reliable definition of a champion.  | `sales.obj.core.champion`, `sales.obj.core.stakeholder`, `sales.obj.core.decision_maker` |


## How to apply

- Identify the tier the person in front of you is measured on and start there. A user buyer interrupted with strategic narrative concludes you do not understand their job, and they are right.

- Anchor every quantified claim to a baseline the buyer supplied. If the baseline came from your marketing team, the claim is a hypothesis and should be spoken as one.

- Climb tiers WITH the buyer, never on your own. A business case the champion did not co-author gets restated wrongly to the CFO, and you will not be in the room to correct it.

- Test the climb by asking the champion to explain the case back to you with the deck closed. Whatever survives that is the case; the rest is your deck.

- Clear the conformance tier early and in writing. It is the only tier where being late is fatal regardless of how good the rest is.

- Before discounting, check which tier the resistance sits on. Price resistance at the economic tier is an arithmetic problem; price resistance at the personal tier is a fear problem, and a discount makes the second one worse by suggesting the first number was invented.

- Re-run the pyramid after any champion change. Personal value is the least portable tier — it belongs to a person, not to the account.



## Failure modes

- Building the value case alone and presenting it as fact. The buyer's first act is to look for the wrong assumption, and there is always one; the case is then dead and so is your credibility on numbers.

- Quantifying value carefully and then discounting heavily. You have just told the buyer the value number was decoration, and they will apply the same scepticism to the next one.

- Treating the top of the pyramid as the goal. Strategic framing aimed at a technical evaluator reads as evasion of the question they asked.

- Skipping conformance because it is unglamorous. Deals die in security review with a perfect business case attached.

- Confusing personal value with flattery or inducement. Personal value is the champion's genuine professional stake; anything transactional is a different conversation with a compliance function attached to it.

- Letting the case go stale. Baselines move — a reorganisation can hand the pain to somebody who has not agreed it exists.



## Limits

- Requires a quantifiable baseline. In a genuinely new category the buyer has no current-state numbers to anchor against, and the economic tier degenerates into arithmetic performed on invented inputs — which a CFO detects immediately.

- Assumes an economic buyer exists. In self-serve and card-swipe purchases there is no P&L conversation to have, and tiers four and five are dead weight.

- Says nothing about whether the buyer will act. A large, well-evidenced value gap with no compelling event sits open indefinitely; pair this with sales.mm.core.status_quo_bias.

- Value above the switching cost is necessary and not sufficient. Buyers routinely decline a positive-NPV change because the disruption lands on a team that did not ask for it.

- Where price is set by a framework or a published rate card, the economic tier is not a persuasion surface — it is a compliance exercise.



## Variants by model or offering

| Applies to | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `sales.model.plg` | The pyramid collapses to conformance and functional value during acquisition, and is only rebuilt at the expansion conversation. Value must be self-evident inside the product in a single session.  | Nobody reads a business case before signing up for a trial. The economic tier becomes relevant when Finance notices the aggregate card spend, which is an expansion event, not an acquisition one.  |
| `sales.model.enterprise_sales` | All six tiers are in play simultaneously with different owners, and the conformance tier is staffed by people who can say no and never yes.  | Eight to fifteen people evaluate on different criteria. A single-tier narrative will be correct for one of them and wrong for the rest.  |
| `sales.model.government_sales` | The personal tier is not available and should not be sought. Strategic value means a published policy objective, and economic value means the evaluation formula in the tender.  | Probity rules make individual benefit a disqualifying conversation, and the scoring weights are published, so the economic tier is arithmetic rather than persuasion.  |
| `sales.model.channel_sales` | A second pyramid exists for the partner — margin, attach rate, services drag, competitive protection — and it is evaluated before the end customer's pyramid ever gets built.  | The partner is a buyer of your programme, not a distribution pipe. A partner who cannot see their own economic tier will not carry yours.  |
| `sales.offering.service` | Economic value is staged into a delivery plan with dated milestones, because most of it is realised after signature.  | For services the value is produced by work not yet done. An undated benefit claim in a services proposal is a claim about a team the buyer has not met.  |
| `sales.model.smb_sales` | The economic tier is the owner's cash and the payback horizon is months, not years. Tiers three to six collapse into one person.  | In an owner-led purchase the operational, economic, strategic and personal tiers are all held by the same head, and a multi-year NPV argument reads as a way of avoiding the price.  |
